headline: Models of unobserved zeros, lineage geometry and reversible mutations refine inference
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: Three new methods target sampling zeros, massive CRISPR lineages and mutation reversions, where simpler models would distort networks, trees or transmission links.
synthesis: The common thread is modeling a hidden data-generating component explicitly rather than treating observed values at face value. TestNet-PA models sampling zeros in microbial presence-absence data with an EM-based quasi-likelihood, aiming at better FDR control in co-occurrence networks. HERACLES optimizes hyperbolic cell embeddings under a quartet-based composite likelihood to reconstruct massive CRISPR lineage-recording phylogenies. VENAS2 allows bidirectional mutations in spatiotemporal evolutionary networks, revealing SARS-CoV-2 reversions and hidden M. tuberculosis transmission links. The items differ in data type and scale, but each replaces a simplifying assumption with an explicit latent or structural model to improve downstream inference.
